title: Ajay Pal v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of on the same terms as Ramavtar Singh; remaining billing computation relegated to Clause 6.5, with no coercive action until a speaking order on any objection.
headnote: A Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court disposed of a writ disputing a domestic electricity bill on the same terms as the coordinate-bench order in Ramavtar Singh (9 December 2022). Remaining computation disputes are to be raised before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if an objection is filed, no coercive measures until that objection is decided by a reasoned speaking order.
facts: Ajay Pal challenged the correctness of a domestic electricity bill for account 781703164925 at Sub-Division EDSD-II Ghiror, District Mainpuri. Both sides agreed the facts were similar to Ramavtar Singh v. State of U.P. (Writ-C No. 34797 of 2022, 9 December 2022), where a Consumer Forum had set aside earlier bills and directed a surcharge-free average-rate revision from 2013, the department had issued a revised bill, and recovery was challenged without citation particulars.

holding_units.holding: A writ disputing the correctness of an electricity bill is not a fit case for interference on the computation itself where remaining billing disputes lie under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer may object to the current computation before the Executive Engineer under that clause; if such an objection is filed, no coercive measures shall be taken until it is disposed of by a reasoned speaking order under intimation to the consumer.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench refused merits interference on the disputed bill and disposed of the writ on the Ramavtar Singh terms, sending remaining computation to Clause 6.5.
